title: Winnecomac / Commack
summary: Winnecomac is the older placename behind Commack, a hamlet spanning Huntington and Smithtown.
introduction_content: Winnecomac is the longer form behind Comac or Commack, with variants including Winecomack, Weno Comack, Wenecomack, Wenea-Commack, and the cross-reference form Wynycomic.
history_content: The name is tied to a tract conveyed by Secatogue people to John Skidmore and John Whitman of Huntington. The modern map point uses Commack as a broad approximate anchor for the placename.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as "a pleasant field," "good land," or "fine country," from elements meaning pleasant or fine and a place, field, or dwelling. Wynycomic is treated as a cross-reference form.

Why Place Names Matter

“Traditional Place Names for Indigenous people have varied, thoughtful and deep meanings.”

— First Nations Education Steering Committee and First Nations Schools Association, BC First Peoples 12 Teacher Resource Guide: The Power of Names (2023), Unit 4, sample responses
preservation_content: The older Winnecomac spellings are connected with modern Commack, while the colonial record context is preserved separately through historic moments.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement in modern Commack, spanning Huntington and Smithtown. Coordinates are approximate and not exact historic deed boundaries.
